title: Pot the object ball in the taped corner pocket of a 7 ft table: one hand is the bridge, the other strokes the cue
instruction: Pot the yellow ball in the corner pocket marked with white tape, striking only the white ball, once, with the cue.
context: A pool shot is recognised from a ten-second clip, and most people have tried one. The robot plays it at the corner of a full-size 7 ft bar table with regulation balls and a 48 in shorty cue, as a player does: one hand forms the bridge that holds the shaft on the aim line while it slides, and the other strokes the cue straight through it, hitting the cue ball near its centre in one contact at the right pace. Aim is physical: the cue ball must reach the ghost-ball point for a 35 degree cut. Too soft stops short, too hard follows the ball into the pocket, and pushing the ball with the cue is a foul.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Near-left corner of a 7 ft bar table (39 x 78 in field, green cloth 7 cm above the arm-base plane, 2 in cushions, 4 in wood rails, 85 mm corner pocket openings): near cushion nose at x 29, left cushion nose at y 65. White cue ball 57 mm, 170 g, on a spot at (42.3, 35.9); yellow 1 ball on a spot at (39.0, 52.6). White tape on both rails of the near-left corner pocket (the target). Action ACTO48 48 in shorty cue (510 g) lies on the near rail, tip to the left, balance point at y = -55. Arms in the ready pose.
scoring: Latched over the trial, from video. 1.0: yellow ball drops into the taped pocket, white ball stays on the table, the cue touched the white ball in exactly one strike. 0.5: yellow in another pocket, or at rest with its centre within 10 cm (ruler) of the taped pocket's corner. 0.25: white ball touched the yellow. Scratch (white ball potted or off the table) caps at 0.25. 0: no strike; two strikes (contacts over 30 ms apart); a push (tip stays on the ball over 70 ms, 2+ frames at 30 fps); a gripper or arm touched a ball; the cue touched the yellow ball; white never touched yellow.
reset_notes: Run at a real 7 ft bar or home table (README); the arms stand at the near rail on a stand, bases 7 cm below the cloth. Balls back on their spot stickers; cue back on the near rail at its pen-marked balance point. Chalk the tip before the session, not between trials.
fidelity: Approximate. Table: fixed boxes, a 7 cm bed with six square pocket openings, square cushions (restitution 0.75), wood rails. Balls: solid spheres (ball-ball restitution 0.93, cloth friction 0.2), rolling resistance as damping. Cue: one rigid body, sphere tip (friction 0.6), smooth shaft that slides through the pinch bridge, butt for the grip; taper in two steps. Slow tip impacts are nearly inelastic in PhysX, so the simulated stroke is faster than a real one. No swerve or nap.
